script:
Roth or traditional 401(k)?
Here's exactly how to choose.
It comes down to when the IRS gets its cut.
Traditional goes in pre-tax, lowering your taxable income today.
Then you pay income tax when you withdraw in retirement.
Roth goes in after tax and grows tax-free.
After age 59 and a half and five years, qualified withdrawals come out federal tax-free.
Now here's the crazy part most people miss.
Say you have $10,000 before taxes, and it grows five times by retirement.
If you're in the 22% federal bracket today and 22% later, both accounts tie.
Traditional grows to $50,000, minus 22% tax, leaving $39,000.
Roth pays 22% upfront, so $7,800 grows five times to $39,000 tax-free.
Exact same money.
Now watch when your bracket changes.
In the 12% bracket today and 22% in retirement?
Roth pays 12% upfront, so $8,800 grows to $44,000 tax-free instead of $39,000.
Flip it, 22% today to 12% later, and traditional wins by $5,000.
So three questions decide it for you.
One, is your tax bracket lower now or in retirement?
Lower now usually favors Roth, higher now favors traditional.
Two, can you take a smaller paycheck today for tax-free money later?
Three, do you want tax flexibility in retirement?
Roth 401(k)s have no lifetime required minimum distributions.
And if your job offers both, you can split contributions up to the annual limit.
Do your own research.
Which one are you using?
Let me know below, and if you're looking to grow your net worth, follow me.
